title: Remaining concupiscence is morally blameworthy and to be crucified
source_text: XXX. Porro hanc concupiscentiam, qualis in ipsis renatis remanet, non negant legi divinae repugnare, quatenus incitat ad ea quae lege prohibentur, & retrahit ab iis quae lex divina jubet. Itaque fatentur illam esse aliquid illaudabile & vituperabile, adeoque defectum, vitium, & malum morale, cui obstinendum sit quodque frenandum atque cohibendum, imo destruendum & crucifigendum est. Qua in re fidelibus sedulo laborandum & connitendum censent, quoque plus in hoc opere processerint, eo majorem fore ipsorum perfectionem atque sanctimoniam.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover they do not deny that this concupiscence, as it remains in the regenerate themselves, is repugnant to the divine law, inasmuch as it incites to things the law forbids and draws back from things the divine law commands. And so they confess it to be something unpraiseworthy and blameworthy, and thus a defect, vice, and moral evil, which is to be opposed and which must be bridled and restrained, indeed destroyed and crucified. In which matter they judge the faithful must labor and strive diligently, and the further they have advanced in this work, the greater will be their perfection and sanctity.
pass_b_english: Rome grants remaining concupiscence opposes the law and is moral vice to bridle, destroy, and crucify.
Progress in that fight marks greater perfection and sanctity.
